question.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the osculating plane for a curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(0,1,1)$ where $t=0$, given that

$$
T(0)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(\,i+\,j+\,k),\,N(0)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\,i-\,j).
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of the point $P(0,1,1)$ is $p=⟨0,1,1⟩.$

To find the equation of the osculating plane, we need to find a vector that's perpendicular to it. To do that, we find the cross product of the unit tangent $T(0)$ and the principal normal $N(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\times N(0) & =(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}(\,i+\,j+\,k))\times (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\,i-\,j)) \\  & =(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}(i+j-2\,k)\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are interested only in the direction of the above vector, let's write our perpendicular vector $n$ as 

$$
n=\sqrt{6}\cdot (T(0)\times N(0))=i+j-2\,k=⟨1,1,-2⟩.
$$

Finally, let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ denote the position vector of a general point on the osculating plane. Since the plane is perpendicular to $n$ and passes through the tip of the position vector $p$, its Cartesian equation can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}(⟨x,y,z⟩-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,-2⟩ & =⟨0,1,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,-2⟩ \\ 1\cdot x+1\cdot y+(-2)\cdot z & =-1 \\ x+y-2z & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
